sections.h2: How do I sell a house fast in Nixa, MO?
sections.html:
Nixa owners can hire an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash purchase, and any buyer who intends to rent the house out will meet the city's rental inspection. Cash tends to be quickest for a house that needs work, while an agent listing tends to bring the top price for one that does not.

Nixa grew quickly, from 12,124 residents in 2000 to 23,257 in 2020, and many streets are lined with houses built in that stretch. With that much similar stock, a plain house competes on price and condition. Where the house is a worn rental, a vacancy or an inherited property, an as-is buyer can spare you repairs and showings.

  • Agent listing: more exposure and more preparation, then a wait while the buyer's lender finishes.
  • Owner sale: you keep the agent's share and manage the contract yourself.
  • Cash purchase: the house goes as it stands, on a closing date you pick.

Judge each offer by the amount left after repairs, fees and carrying costs.

sections.h2: What is the town of Nixa like?
sections.html:
Nixa is a Christian County city about six miles south of Springfield, six miles west of Ozark, eight miles north of Highlandville and eight miles east of Clever. It rests on and around seven hills.

The area began as a crossroads where teamsters hauling freight between Springfield and Arkansas stopped, and the settlement was first called Faughts. Nicholas A. Inman, a blacksmith, opened a shop in 1852, and the town's name combines the word Nix, offered because the place was nothing but a crossroads, with the A from Inman's middle name. The village incorporated in 1902 and became a fourth-class city in 1946. Each May, Main Street hosts Sucker Day, a tradition begun in 1957 by Mayor Finis Gold.

Local employers include Accurate Plastics, Snyders Equipment Company, a division of New York Air Brake, Aire-Master and Nixa Hardware, which opened in 1899. In 2017 the city completed the largest solar farm in Missouri at that time, a 72-acre array of 33,288 panels that supplies an estimated 9 percent of the city's power. A new owner opens a utilities account directly with Nixa Utilities.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Nixa housing?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 23,257 people in Nixa, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,597, which is 14.4 percent above the 2020 base. Lee's Summit, Liberty and Maryland Heights all grew more slowly.

The city holds 2,553.7 people per square mile, denser than Lee's Summit, Liberty or Maryland Heights, and 27.6 percent of residents are under 18. A three-bedroom house with a yard near a school has an obvious audience. About 91.7 percent of residents were in the same house a year earlier, so households tend to stay, and few homes come to market at any one time.

Nixa Public Schools serves the city. It runs four elementary schools for kindergarten through fourth grade: Helen-Matthews, Espy, Century and High Pointe, which opened in August 2007 on the highest elevation in Christian County.

Inman Intermediate and Summit Intermediate cover fifth and sixth grades, and Nixa Junior High and Nixa Public High School follow. John Thomas School of Discovery is a magnet school for kindergarten through sixth grade. Ozarks Technical Community College has its Richwood Valley campus in the Nixa ZIP code. Put the elementary school name in your listing, since young families search by school.

sections.h2: What is Nixa's rental inspection rule, and does it affect a sale?
sections.html:
Nixa requires a rental unit that is at least one year old to pass an inspection before a new tenant moves in and before utilities go into the tenant's name. It matters to a seller when the buyer plans to rent the house out.

  • Fee: $25 per inspection, paid before the visit through a link the city emails after you submit the request form.
  • Notice: 24 hours; same-day inspections are not available. Inspections run 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, in a morning or afternoon window.
  • Who can schedule: only a landlord or property manager.
  • Penalty: $50 if a tenant moves in, or receives keys, before a passed inspection. An early move-in inspection costs $75.
  • Failed inspection: 90 days to make repairs and call for a re-inspection, after which a new inspection and $25 fee apply.

The house must be empty, clean and move-in ready. The inspector looks at the roof and gutters, smoke detectors on every story, GFCI protection in bathrooms, water heater safety valves, the windows and doors, weeds above 12 inches and other items on the city's checklist. Planning and Development answers questions at (417) 725-5850.

sections.h2: Can I run a short-term rental in Nixa?
sections.html:
Nixa regulates short-term residential rentals in its code, and the rules changed after Missouri House Bill 1662 took effect in June 2022. Ask Planning and Development which version applies before you advertise one.

According to a May 2024 staff report, the city's first ordinance dated from August 2019 and allowed such rentals only in a primary residence with a special use permit. Staff proposed two categories: a primary residence rental, which needs only a city business license, and a non-primary residence rental, which would be subject to a ban on using accessory structures, an annual rental inspection and a 150-foot separation from other short-term rentals. Anyone buying an investment house for this use should ask the city whether the proposal was adopted as written.

sections.h2: How do Christian County records and taxes work for a Nixa sale?
sections.html:
Christian County keeps the land records, and its Recorder of Deeds office is in the Historical Courthouse at 100 W. Church Street, Room 104, in Ozark. A title company ordinarily records the deed after closing.

The office takes walk-in, mail and electronic filings, with eRecording routed through a vendor such as iCounty Technologies. Staff cannot supply forms, notarize or give legal advice. Missouri Senate Bill 938 adjusted recording fees on August 28, 2026, so ask the office for the present charge. A free service at deedwatch.com emails an owner whenever a document is recorded under a registered name.

The assessor covers 564 square miles holding over 42,951 real estate parcels, and the county's total assessed value passed $2 billion for 2025. Homes are assessed at 19 percent of market value, and the levy comes from thirteen school districts, eight road districts, ten cities, nine fire districts and other bodies, so the districts at your address set your bill. Ask the Collector's Office in Room 101 of the courthouse for the amount and due date. The county also announced a Senior Citizen Real Estate Tax Credit: first-time applications open March 1, 2027 and close June 15, 2027 for owners who are at least 62 by December 31, 2026 and who have lived in the home since at least June 29, 2026 and have paid their 2026 taxes.

faqs.q: Does Nixa inspect a house when it is sold?
faqs.a: Only if the buyer plans to rent it out. Nixa's program inspects rental units before each new tenant moves in, for $25, and a landlord cannot let a tenant move in until the unit has passed.

faqs.q: What is the penalty if a tenant moves into a Nixa rental before it passes inspection?
faqs.a: $50. An early move-in inspection costs $75. A landlord who allows more than one violation can be summoned to Municipal Court.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a house in Nixa?
faqs.a: At the Christian County Recorder of Deeds in the Historical Courthouse at 100 W. Church Street, Room 104, in Ozark. Your title company can file it for you.

faqs.q: Can I run an Airbnb in my Nixa house?
faqs.a: Possibly. Nixa has short-term rental rules that were rewritten after Missouri House Bill 1662. A primary residence rental needs a city business license, and the rules for other houses may add an annual inspection and a 150-foot spacing requirement. Confirm the current version with Planning and Development.

faqs.q: How do I set up utilities after buying a house in Nixa?
faqs.a: The buyer opens an account with Nixa Utilities at 715 W Mt Vernon St with a residential application, photo ID, information on every adult living there and a deposit. Rental properties also need a passed rental inspection.
